questions.q: A value that describes a sample, like x̄, is called a...
questions.why: Statistics describe samples (Latin letters). Parameters describe populations (Greek letters, like μ).

questions.q: A transit survey conducted only at bus stops overestimates transit use. This is...
questions.why: Bias is systematic and comes from how the sample was collected. Unlike sampling error, it doesn't shrink with a bigger sample.

questions.q: What happens to sampling error as the sample size increases?
questions.why: Sampling error can't be eliminated, but it shrinks with larger samples and can be quantified with probability.

questions.q: Why are probability samples required for the inference methods in this course?
options: Every member has a known, nonzero chance of selection, so we can quantify how representative the sample is
They always have 30 or more observations
questions.why: With convenience or volunteer samples, there's no way to know how representative the sample is.

questions.q: A statewide survey samples separately within urban, suburban and rural counties. This is...
questions.why: Stratified sampling takes a random sample within each group so every group is represented.

questions.q: Randomly selecting 20 census block groups and surveying households within them is...
questions.why: Cluster sampling is cheaper, but usually less precise because members of the same cluster tend to be similar.

questions.q: Placing sample locations on a regular grid gives even coverage, but it can...
options: miss patterns smaller than the grid spacing or that line up with the grid
only be used for areal data
questions.why: Random spatial sampling is the one that can leave gaps or clusters by chance.

questions.q: Why do sample points close together provide less independent information?
options: Because of spatial dependence, nearby points tend to have similar values
questions.why: This is one reason systematic and stratified designs are often preferred for spatial sampling.

questions.q: Why could EPA and PurpleAir monitors give a biased picture of air quality across North Carolina?
options: Neither network is a random sample of locations; they cluster in cities and wealthier neighborhoods
questions.why: Much spatial data comes from where agencies or people chose to put monitors, not from a planned sampling design.

questions.q: What is the difference between the standard deviation and the standard error?
options: The SD describes how much individual observations vary; the SE describes how much the sample mean varies from sample to sample
The SD only applies to proportions
questions.why: The SE is the standard deviation of the sampling distribution, σ divided by the square root of n.

questions.q: To cut the standard error in half, you need a sample that is...
questions.why: Because n is under a square root, halving the SE takes four times the sample size.

questions.q: The Central Limit Theorem says that, for a large enough sample, the sampling distribution of the mean is approximately normal...
options: only if the population is normal
regardless of the shape of the population distribution
questions.why: That's why we can use the normal distribution even for skewed variables like income. A common rule of thumb is n of 30 or more.

questions.q: Why do confidence intervals for a mean usually use the t-distribution instead of z?
options: We almost never know σ and estimate it with s, which adds uncertainty
questions.why: The t-distribution has heavier tails, giving a wider interval. With more degrees of freedom it approaches the normal.

questions.q: A correct interpretation of a 95% confidence interval is...
options: there's a 95% probability the parameter is in this interval
if we repeated the sampling many times, about 95% of the intervals would contain the true parameter
95% of the data fall in the interval
questions.why: The parameter is fixed; it is either in this interval or not. The 95% describes how reliable the method is.

questions.q: Which change makes a confidence interval narrower?
options: Raising the confidence level from 95% to 99%
questions.why: A larger n shrinks the standard error. A higher confidence level and more variability both widen the interval.

questions.q: Two census tracts have ACS median incomes of $52,000 and $55,000. Before saying the second is higher, you should...
options: check whether their margins of error (confidence intervals) overlap
take the mean of the two
questions.why: The ACS is a sample survey with 90% margins of error, and they can be large for small areas like tracts.
